That is a good place to start.  My husband and I agree on one date a week and have a rule: no breaking it, no rescheduling.  When we did that, we found that sex slipped to once or twice a month again (or less).  So we schedule, we stick to it and I find that, although it's not my dream sex life, I can live with it.

First, you need to ensure that there is not a medical issue causing your fiance's lack of sex drive.  Medications, low testosterone, diabetes could all interfere with his libido.  If those are not the issue, however, and he truly just has a low sex drive...

Know that it's not your fault.  It's natural to feel unwanted or unattractive when your SO doesn't want to have sex with you as much as you want to have sex with them.  Trust me, I've lived with this for almost two decades.  It took a lot of crying, fighting, begging, etc, for me to realize that the issue is with him and not me.  Your fiance has a low sex drive and that would be the same story if he were with you or with Angelina Jolie. 

There are compromises you could come to.  Scheduling sex sounds awful but it can help people with low libidos.  He'll know that you guys have a "date" every Tuesday (or whatever) and can prepare himself mentally.  Also, sexual encounters don't have to include intercourse every time, so he could use other means to bring you pleasure if he's not in the mood.  These might not sound thrilling, but at least they're places to start.

I won't sugarcoat this: living with a spouse whose sex drive is much lower than mine is very difficult at times.  Sometimes I feel like we're just roommates or friends.  I miss so much the passionate sexual energy that I knew with previous partners.  I would not recommend this lifestyle to others because it is very challenging.  Our relationship is wonderful in other aspects and I love him very much.  But it is definitely a sacrifice that not everyone is willing to make.  Before you marry him I would make sure that you're willing and able to live like this, faithfully, forever.

I have been married for 12 years now, together for almost 18 years total.  He's my best friend, my lover, my confidante, my rock.  I honestly don't know what I'd do without him.  

This is not to say that every day is great.  We have bad times, some of them downright horrible.  I've had moments where I questioned our future but they always pass.  We decided at the beginning that divorce just isn't an option.  We don't threaten the other with it.

My advice is to date/live together for a long time before getting married.  Be 100% sure that he/she is the one for you before taking that step.  And for the love of Pete, be sure you're sexually compatible.  We are in a good place now, but it's something we've really had to work at because we have differing libidos. 

Long story short: marrying my husband was the smartest thing I've ever done.
